title: Make a transfer survive being a deadlock victim

blocks.text: Wallet transfers run all day; at midnight an interest job adds a little to every wallet, one transaction per batch, in its own order. Since the job moved earlier, a few transfers a night fail with SQLState 40001. Customers retry by hand, and support would like that to stop. A first attempt at an automatic retry made the nightly totals stop adding up, and a transfer to a wallet that is already near its limit now hammers the database three times before failing.

Finish `transfer(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/Transfers.java`, using `debit` and `credit`. The table's `CHECK` keeps every balance between 0 and 1000. When you're done, a transfer that collides with the interest job still completes with the right balances, and a transfer the database refuses for its own rules fails at once and changes nothing. About twelve lines.
The tests run on an in-memory H2 database. They start the interest job's transaction before the transfer and use the `Pause` after the debit to make the two cross.

cases.says: a transfer nobody interferes with debits one wallet, credits the other and commits
a transfer chosen as a deadlock victim leaves the total of the two wallets as it should be
a transfer chosen as a deadlock victim still moves the money and returns normally
a transfer the database refuses for a broken rule fails after one attempt and changes nothing

origin.section: On H2, a Lock Timeout Fails One Statement; a Deadlock Rolls Back the Whole Transaction

concepts: After SQLState 40001 the transaction is gone, so it is retried from its first statement, and failures that a retry cannot fix are not retried.
